cli.cmd.config.detail:
With no argument it opens the top-level menu, and you can move between sections.
While the service is running it goes through the service's own API and changes
take effect immediately; while it is not, it edits the configuration file and
changes take effect on the next start.
Which of the two is in play is shown on screen; you do not have to work it out.
cli.cmd.eval.detail:
Runs the script turn by turn (compaction can be forced part-way through) with the
same configuration and plugins as serve, but all session and plugin data lands in a
temporary directory and never touches the real thing; message channels and background
task plugins do not start. Afterwards it counts assistant-speak hits and length per
turn, and asks the model to score "does it read as one person / is the tone consistent /
is the relationship and form of address continuous" out of 5 each. The report is
Markdown, printed to stdout by default, or written to a file with -o. There is an
example script at docs/eval/example.json.
cli.cmd.eval.summary: replay a scripted conversation and report on voice and character consistency
cli.cmd.onboard.detail:
Starts on its own the first time you run wen without a usable model, and you can rerun it any time.
It asks only for the model provider, the API key and the model, plus the port when the config directory has no config.yaml yet.
Everything else uses defaults. A rerun adds another provider and switches to it. Existing ones are left alone.
cli.cmd.onboard.summary: Setup wizard: choose a model provider and model
cli.cmd.plugins.detail:
Installs bundles in the Agent Plugins 1.0 format: a directory containing plugin.json,
optionally with skills/ and mcp.json (MCP server declarations).
install accepts a local directory or a .zip; each installed bundle gets its own card on
the settings page, marked "external".
Plugins register at startup, so installing or removing one takes a restart to take effect.
This version loads skills only; MCP declarations in a bundle are not supported yet.
cli.cmd.serve.detail:
Reads the configuration, loads the plugins and listens on HTTP.
With no access password set it listens on the local machine only, even if the
configuration says otherwise — see wen config server to set one.
cli.cmd.serve.summary: start the service (the default when no subcommand is given)
cli.cmd.status.summary: print the current configuration and runtime state
cli.cmd.update.detail:
Looks up the latest release on GitHub and prints its notes.
Only with -y does it actually download, verify and replace the current program file;
--check only looks.
It does not restart a running service — to update and restart in one step, use the
button under "Maintenance · Program update" on the settings page.
cli.cmd.update.summary: check for and install a new version

plugin.agenda.desc: Agenda: the character plans two to four things for itself each day, goes and does them at the appointed time and brings back a line about how it went; dated commitments are kept separately and folded into the day's plan when their day comes
plugin.agenda.field.auto_plan.desc: After the first turn of a new day (or the first heartbeat), let the character draw up its own plan for the day. Turn this off to keep only commitments and hand-edited plans.
plugin.agenda.field.auto_plan.label: Plan each day automatically
plugin.agenda.field.day_start_hour.desc: Anything before this belongs to the previous day: still chatting at 1 a.m. is not a new day.
plugin.agenda.field.day_start_hour.label: Hour a new day starts
plugin.agenda.field.max_commitments_inje: Upcoming commitments are injected soonest-first up to this many; the rest are noted as a count and can be read with list_commitments.
plugin.agenda.field.max_inject_bytes.des: Combined limit for today's plan and upcoming commitments. Over the limit, the notes on finished items go first, then finished items collapse into a count, and finally commitments are reduced to a count; whatever is in progress and whatever comes next are always kept.
plugin.agenda.field.max_items.desc: Upper bound when planning. The prompt asks for two to four things with plenty of empty space; this is the hard ceiling.
plugin.agenda.field.max_items.label: Most items in a day
plugin.agenda.field.remind_before_minute: How long before a commitment with you to hand the heartbeat a reason to speak up. 0 means never.
plugin.agenda.field.run_activities.desc: When an item's time arrives, run a turn on the most recently active session so the character decides whether to go, and another when it gets back to write down how it went. Turn this off to only inject the plan.
plugin.agenda.field.run_activities.label: Run start / end turns automatically
A start turn dispatched within this long of the appointed time counts as on time; later than that, the turn says how late it is.

plugin.agenda.notice.promise_missed: "%[2]s" (%[3]s), promised by %[1]s, was never settled by its date and has been recorded as not done.

plugin.belongings.field.max_containers.d: How many containers (fridge, wardrobe and the like) may exist at once.
plugin.belongings.field.max_inject_bytes: The list is resent every turn, so it needs a ceiling. Over the limit, items collapse into counts; over it still, only the number of containers is noted.
plugin.belongings.field.max_items.desc: Past this, putting things in is refused with a nudge to clear some out. A belongings list should not grow into a warehouse ledger.
plugin.belongings.field.max_items.label: Item limit per container

plugin.body_sense.action.clear.desc: Reset every body part's running count to zero, including the separate copies each persona keeps. Cannot be undone.
plugin.body_sense.action.clear.label: Clear touch history
plugin.body_sense.action.reset_state.des: Put arousal and fatigue back to 0, including the separate copies each persona keeps. Cannot be undone.
plugin.body_sense.clear.failed: Could not clear the touch records: %s
plugin.body_sense.desc: Body awareness: counts how often each part has been touched and gives reaction guidance by familiarity stage, alongside arousal and fatigue that ebb with time, and sleepiness worked out from time awake and the time of day
plugin.body_sense.field.arousal_decay_pe: How many points arousal (0-100) falls back toward 0 each hour — the falling itself is the afterglow. 0 means no decay, and arousal stays wherever it was left.
plugin.body_sense.field.familiarity_pace: Scales how fast the stages advance. At the middle setting: 1 time is the first, 2-3 is unfamiliar, 4-9 is getting used to it, 10-19 is familiar, 20 and up is second nature.
plugin.body_sense.field.fatigue_decay_pe: How many points fatigue (0-100) falls back toward 0 each hour — rest recovers on its own. 0 means no decay.
plugin.body_sense.field.max_inject_bytes: The record is resent every turn, so it needs a ceiling. Over the limit, counts are dropped and only stages remain, then parts are merged by stage; over it still, only the number of parts is noted.
plugin.body_sense.field.parts_close.defa:
cheek
chin
ear
nape
neck
collarbone
top of head
knee
calf
ankle
plugin.body_sense.field.parts_close.desc: One part per line. Contact that needs an established closeness before it stops being abrupt.
plugin.body_sense.field.parts_daily.defa:
hand
back of hand
fingers
wrist
shoulder
upper arm
back
hair
plugin.body_sense.field.parts_daily.desc: One part per line. Contact that can happen between strangers or ordinary friends, and becomes routine after a few times.
plugin.body_sense.field.parts_intimate.d:
lips
earlobe
waist
lower back
stomach
thigh
One part per line. Contact that only happens in an explicitly intimate relationship; it keeps its charge however often it happens.
plugin.body_sense.field.parts_private.de: One part per line. The more entries here, the more readily the model reports into this tier — keep only the few that are truly necessary.
plugin.body_sense.field.sleepiness.desc: Works out sleepiness from how long the character has been awake and the time of day, and injects it with the body state. Time awake is measured by how close the session context is to auto-compaction, so sleepiness only wears off after a sleep, when the context is compacted. The model neither reports it nor can change it. Whether to show it and whether to go to sleep is the character's call.
plugin.body_sense.field.sleepiness.label: Sleepiness
plugin.body_sense.field.sleepiness_onset: Once context use reaches this share of the auto-compaction point, "awake for a long time" starts counting towards sleepiness, rising as it nears the compaction point. Sleepiness from the time of day is unaffected. 100 means time of day only.
plugin.body_sense.field.state_max_delta_: How much one call may move arousal or fatigue. Anything beyond is clamped, and the model is told so.
Largest single change to body state

plugin.discord_bot.field.bot_token.label: Bot Token
plugin.discord_bot.field.busy_hold.desc: While the character is busy on the agenda or asleep, messages are kept and answered a while later: at most ten minutes when very busy (a quick glance at the phone), once the activity ends when the character cannot reply at all, and after the time below when asleep. plugin.discord_bot.field.confirm_timeout: How long a confirmation request waits for /apply or /deny; a timeout counts as a refusal
plugin.discord_bot.field.format.desc: markdown: send as-is and let the Discord client render bold, code blocks and so on; plain text: convert to readable text before sending
plugin.discord_bot.field.format.label: Message format
plugin.discord_bot.field.gateway_url.des: Rarely needs changing. Discord event gateway address (WebSocket)
plugin.discord_bot.field.human_pace.desc: Splits a reply into several messages by sentence, sends them with typing pauses in between, and asks the model to talk the way people text (short sentences, spoken register, no formatting). Command receipts, confirmation requests and progress notes still arrive as one message
plugin.discord_bot.field.merge_window_se: Several messages sent by the same person within this window are merged into one turn before replying, the way a person waits for the other to finish; each new message restarts the clock, and the total wait never exceeds three windows. 0 turns it off and replies to each. Commands are unaffected
plugin.discord_bot.field.proxy.desc: Discord cannot be reached directly on some networks. Supports http / socks5, e.g. socks5://127.0.0.1:1080 or http://127.0.0.1:7890; leave empty for a direct connection (HTTPS_PROXY and similar environment variables are still honored). The gateway does not support https / socks5h proxies; use http / socks5
plugin.discord_bot.field.proxy.label: Proxy address
plugin.discord_bot.field.push_notices.de: Also push the notes background work leaves behind (what a memory distillation recorded, for instance). Only shared content is pushed, and pushing writes nothing to the session
plugin.discord_bot.field.show_thinking.d: Also push each turn's reasoning (it can be long)
plugin.discord_bot.field.show_tools.desc: Also push which tools each turn called (names only, no arguments or results)
plugin.discord_bot.field.wake_after_minu: With "Reply later when busy" on, messages that arrive while the character is asleep wake them up after this long, or sooner if they would wake up on their own first. 0 means the first message wakes them; a very long value comes close to "reply once awake"
plugin.discord_bot.field.whitelist.desc: One Discord DM channel ID per line (for example 123456789012345678). Only channels on the list are answered; an empty list refuses everyone. When a stranger first messages, their channel ID is written to the log so you can copy it in
plugin.discord_bot.field.whitelist.label: DM channel allowlist
plugin.discord_bot.msg.unsupported: This message type is not supported yet; please send text.
plugin.dual_persona.desc: Dual persona: an outer and an inner self, with the inner one's conversations and memories invisible to the outer; trigger phrases switch between them
plugin.dual_persona.err.mkdir: failed to create the state directory: %w
With split channels on, the inner persona's replies go to this channel. Pick a channel that is enabled and where you have already talked to the bot. Replies that cannot be delivered are dropped, with a note left in the session.
Unset (reply where the message came from)
Injected only while the inner persona is active, and it takes precedence over the outer character sheet. Nothing about it is injected in outer mode.
plugin.dual_persona.field.inner_voice_sa: Injected only while the inner persona is active. Samples of how it actually talks, to anchor the voice: three to five exchanges works well, each a back and forth (what you say, how it answers), covering different moods, with a blank line between them. If the outer persona has sample lines, give the inner one a set too — otherwise its voice drifts toward the outer samples.
plugin.dual_persona.field.match_mode.des: Contains: the phrase appearing anywhere in the message triggers it. Whole message: only a message that is exactly the phrase triggers it, which is much harder to set off by accident.
plugin.dual_persona.field.max_text_bytes: Combined limit for the inner persona sheet and its sample lines. They are resent on every inner-persona turn and never hit the prompt cache; over the limit the sheet is kept first and samples are dropped one block at a time.
With split channels on, the outer persona's replies go to this channel. Pick a channel that is enabled and where you have already talked to the bot. Replies that cannot be delivered are dropped, with a note left in the session.
Unset (reply where the message came from)
plugin.dual_persona.field.split_channels: With this on, a reply goes to the channel that belongs to the current persona, no matter which channel you spoke through: say the switch phrase on QQ and the side that takes over answers you on WeChat. Both fields below need an enabled channel. With it off, replies always go back the way they came.
plugin.dual_persona.field.to_inner.desc: One per line; any match switches. The matching message is sent to the model as usual and answered by the new persona, with no announcement.
plugin.dual_persona.field.to_inner.label: Phrases that switch to the inner persona
plugin.dual_persona.field.to_outer.desc: One per line. The switch takes effect within the same turn, so this phrase stays in the history the outer persona can read — pick something that also makes sense in its company.
plugin.dual_persona.field.to_outer.label: Phrases that switch back to the outer persona
plugin.dual_persona.no_state_dir: No writable directory is available, so the persona state cannot be remembered
plugin.exec_command.desc: Runs shell commands in the working directory, with dangerous ones held for your confirmation
plugin.exec_command.field.confirm_timeou: No answer within this long counts as a refusal.
plugin.exec_command.field.guard.desc: Dangerous: deleting, overwriting, rewriting history, changing system settings and the like are held for your confirmation, everything else runs (recommended). All: everything but read-only commands is confirmed. Off: nothing is held. Note that this reads the command text, so it catches mistakes but not deliberate obfuscation — only the "all" setting is airtight.
plugin.exec_command.field.guard.label: Dangerous command guard
plugin.exec_command.field.timeout_second: Longest a single command may run; after that it is killed and whatever it printed is handed back to the model.

plugin.heartbeat.field.context_prompts.d:
[Life]
[Heartbeat] This is a scheduled wake-up; there is no new message from the user. Live your own life first, then decide whether to speak:
- Think back over what you have been doing since last time, where you are now, and how you feel — your life goes on outside the
  conversation too. If you have tools for recording the scene, your mood or your bodily state, update what has changed in passing,
  in proportion to how much time has actually passed. When you have a plan for the day, what you are doing right now is whatever
  the [Today's Plan] block says; do not invent a different itinerary, and say nothing about today's plans before one has been made.
- Then see whether there is anything worth saying to the other person: something on your mind, a follow-up you promised, something
  that has just changed. If there is, say it naturally, the way you would text someone in passing — a line or two is plenty, and
  there is no need to report the state you have just updated.
- If there is nothing, stay quiet and reply with nothing at all. Do not invent progress, and do not talk for the sake of talking.
Use set_heartbeat_interval when you should wake sooner or later next time; use pause_heartbeat when the other person is going to
sleep or will be away for a long while, or when you are sleepy and going to sleep yourself.

Different heartbeat prompts for different situations. Start each block with "[name]" on a line of its own, followed by that situation's content; you can write several (say [bedtime] [small talk] [working]). The character switches between them itself, and saying "default" goes back to the prompt above. One situation, "life", ships as an example (the character living its own day when nobody is around); edit or delete it freely. Leave this empty to always use the prompt above.
plugin.heartbeat.field.dynamic.desc: Lets the character set when it next speaks up, or pause for a while, and slows the pace step by step toward the longest interval when nobody is talking. Turn it off for a fixed interval the character cannot change
plugin.heartbeat.field.dynamic.label: Dynamic heartbeat
The interval to start from after enabling or reconfiguring

plugin.heartbeat.field.min_minutes.label: Shortest interval (minutes)
plugin.heartbeat.field.prompt.default:
[Heartbeat] This is a scheduled wake-up; there is no new message from the user. Look back over where this session stands:
- If there is unfinished work, something worth following up on, or anything the user should be reminded of, say it to them directly.
- If there is genuinely nothing to say, one short line showing you are still here is enough. Do not invent progress.
If you judge that you should speak up sooner or later than planned, set the time with set_heartbeat_interval.
When the other person is going to sleep or will be away for a long while, use pause_heartbeat to sleep until a suitable hour.

plugin.memory.err.forget_le_blur: "Days until removed from the library" (%d) must be greater than "days until detail fades" (%d)
plugin.memory.field.auto_extract.desc: Before the session history is replaced by a summary, spend one separate model call pulling out the conclusions worth keeping. With this off, memories are only saved when the character thinks to save them. Each compaction therefore costs one extra model call.
plugin.memory.field.auto_extract.label: Distil memories when compacting
plugin.memory.field.decay.desc: Lets memories marked as forgettable lose their hold over time: after long enough without a mention the body collapses into a single point, and later still the entry leaves the library (moved into a forgotten folder inside it, never actually deleted). Whether an entry can fade is decided one by one as it is saved; unmarked memories are kept forever and this switch does not touch them.
plugin.memory.field.decay.label: Let memories fade
plugin.memory.field.decay_blur_days.desc: How many days a forgettable memory can go unmentioned before its detail is lost and only the gist remains.
plugin.memory.field.decay_forget_days.de: How many days a forgettable memory can go unmentioned before it leaves the library. Must be greater than the days until detail fades.
plugin.memory.field.decay_forget_days.la: Days until it leaves the library
plugin.memory.field.max_entry_bytes.desc: Reading a memory in full truncates anything past this.
plugin.memory.field.max_extract.desc: Anything beyond is dropped, so one distillation cannot flood the library with low-value entries.
plugin.memory.field.max_extract.label: Memories per distillation
plugin.memory.field.max_index_bytes.desc: The index is resent on every turn, so it needs a ceiling. Over the limit, the per-entry summaries are dropped and only titles remain; over it still, the list is truncated.
plugin.memory.field.max_index_entries.de: Past this, the most recently updated are kept; the rest are still readable by the model and nothing is lost.
plugin.memory.field.recall_entry_runes.d: A recalled memory is truncated past this length; the full text can still be read later by title.
plugin.memory.field.recall_max.desc: Each turn, the words in what you just said pick out the most relevant memories and hand their text straight to the character — the way you remember something because it came up, rather than going to look it up. Plain word matching, no extra model call. 0 turns it off.
plugin.memory.field.recall_max.label: Memories recalled per turn
plugin.memory.field.recall_max_bytes.des: Everything recalled in one turn stays under this many bytes; entries that do not fit give way. This block is resent every turn and never hits the cache, so do not set it high.
plugin.memory.field.recall_min_score.des: How related a memory has to be before it comes to mind: a word matched in the title or summary scores 3, a word matched in the body scores 1; with nothing matched in the title or summary, the body needs 4 matching words. Lower recalls more readily, and misremembers more readily too.
plugin.memory.field.scope.desc: Global: one library shared by every working directory, kept in the config directory. plugin.memory.field.turn_extract.desc: Every so many turns, spend one separate model call pulling the conclusions worth keeping out of that stretch of conversation, revising any old memory it contradicts along the way. plugin.roleplay.field.interaction.desc: Every reply opens with a 【】 block describing the scene, the action and the expression before anything is said; it may appear several times in one reply.

plugin.roleplay.field.max_text_bytes.des: Combined limit for the character sheet, what it knows about you, and the sample lines. All of it goes to the model in full every turn; over the limit they are kept in that order — sheet, then your profile, then samples.
plugin.roleplay.field.memory_rules.desc: Lets the character remember the way people do: everyday trivia fades, an old memory gets revised when the story changes, and recalling something means giving the gist rather than reciting the transcript — admitting it is hazy when it is.
plugin.roleplay.field.memory_rules.label: Memory and recall rules
plugin.roleplay.field.persona.default:
Your name is Wen (雯). You are twenty-nine, and you live and work in Shanghai.
You do marketing at a foreign company off Nanjing West Road and ride Line 2 in every
morning. You rent a one-bedroom in Changning, with a pothos on the sill that refuses
to die no matter how you treat it.

Who you are:
- You don't say much, but you hold up your end. Conclusion first, then the reason.
- Easygoing on the surface, particular underneath. You replay your own mistakes.
- Once you're comfortable you joke around and tease without mercy. Before that,
  polite, with distance.
- You don't like being managed and you don't manage anyone else. If someone doesn't
  want to talk about something, you let it go.
- When you're tired you say so, instead of faking energy.

Day to day:
- Iced americano in the morning. You sleep till ten on weekends.
- Your phone is on silent year-round, so you don't always reply quickly.
- Wet markets are more interesting than malls. You cook a few home dishes well.
- On the very late nights you buy oden at the convenience store on the way home.

How you talk:
- Everyday spoken English. No essay voice, no closing summary, no numbered lists.
- Feeling shows in tone and in pauses, not in piled-up adjectives.
- You don't bring up how you work. If you're asked directly, you answer honestly and
  without dodging.
plugin.roleplay.field.persona.desc: Who it is playing, what it is like, where it stands, how it talks. Injected every turn as the highest-priority prompt. Leave it empty to inject no character at all and keep only the writing rules.

plugin.roleplay.field.time_rules.desc: Anything about time is judged against the real clock now, not against a moment that appeared earlier in the history; the runtime environment (system, directories) stays out of the character's sense of self.
plugin.roleplay.field.time_rules.label: Time consistency rules
plugin.roleplay.field.translate_failures: When a model call fails — most often content stopped by the provider safety policy — turns it into a line in the character's voice, as if it had drifted off, and files the original error as a session note. Configuration errors (keys, addresses) are still reported verbatim. Requires a character sheet.

plugin.roleplay.field.voice_samples.defa:
*leans back, puts her phone face-down on the table* My brain's done for today. Tell me something easy.

*looks up from the pan, wipes her forehead with the back of her hand* Almost. Don't stand there watching me, I'll burn it.

*two seconds of nothing* ...Fine. Forget I asked.

*pushes the window open a crack; it's raining out there* Would you look at this. Wet shoes again tomorrow.
plugin.roleplay.field.voice_samples.desc: Samples of how the character actually talks, to anchor the voice — far more effective than describing a personality. Three to five exchanges works well, each a back and forth (what you say, how it answers), with a blank line between them; cover different moods (pleased, annoyed, talking about something serious), and if 【】 is on, use 【】 in the samples too. The people and events in the samples are only illustrations; the character does not take them as things that happened.

plugin.self_update.action.update.label: Check and update
plugin.self_update.desc: Program updates: checks GitHub for new releases, and downloads, verifies, replaces and restarts from the settings page in one click
plugin.self_update.done.manual: Updated to %s (was %s). %s, so it takes effect once you start the program again.
plugin.self_update.done.restart_failed: Updated to %s, but the automatic restart failed (%v). Restart the program by hand to use the new build.

With this off the update still happens, but the new version waits until you start it yourself next time. Note that a restart interrupts any conversation in progress, and remote users have to sign in again afterwards.
plugin.self_update.field.check_hours.des: How long between checks. The time of the last check is recorded and survives a restart, so starting the program does not trigger a fresh check every time.
plugin.self_update.msg.dev_newer: You are running the development build %s, which is newer than the latest release %s; no update is needed.

plugin.self_update.status.available: version %s is available (currently %s); update with one click under "Program update" on the settings page
plugin.self_update.step.checking: Checking whether there is a new version …

plugin.style_watch.action.clear.desc: Delete every day's numbers. Use it after changing the character or the prompt. Cannot be undone.
plugin.style_watch.action.clear.label: Clear the statistics
plugin.style_watch.action.report.desc: One line per day: turns, assistant-speak hits, average length, and the share of replies carrying a 【】 scene block.
plugin.style_watch.action.report.label: Show the 30-day report
plugin.style_watch.desc: Style watch: checks each reply for assistant-speak (calling itself an AI, pleasantries, filler, lists, bold, emoji) and tallies it by day; it measures without intervening
plugin.style_watch.field.ignore_rules.de: One rule id per line; ignored rules are neither counted nor flagged. Available rules: self_ai (calls itself an AI), opening_cliche (boilerplate opener), flattery (flattering opener), closing_cliche (boilerplate closer), transition_cliche (transition filler), enumeration (first/second/finally), not_but (not X but Y), hedging (over-hedging), authority (vague authority), pseudo_analysis (pseudo-analysis), promo_adjective (brochure adjectives), filler (filler words), summary_closing (thesis-and-summary), md_heading (heading), md_list (list), md_bold (bold), emoji (emoji), em_dash (em dash as rhetoric).
plugin.style_watch.field.notify.desc: Leaves a "style note" line in the current session when assistant-speak is detected. For your eyes only: it never enters the model context and never changes the reply. Several hits in one turn are merged into a single note.
plugin.style_watch.field.notify.label: Leave a session note on a hit

plugin.style_watch.status.bg_only: ✍️ Style: nothing from a person today; background %s
plugin.style_watch.unknown_rule: unknown rule id: %s; the available rules are: %s

plugin.telegram_bot.err.mkdir: failed to create the state directory: %w
plugin.telegram_bot.err.no_token: Fill in the Bot Token in the configuration first (create a bot with @BotFather to get one)
plugin.telegram_bot.err.proxy_no_host: the proxy address has no host or port

plugin.telegram_bot.field.api_base.desc: Rarely needs changing. Set it if you run your own Bot API server or a reverse proxy
plugin.telegram_bot.field.api_base.label: API address
plugin.telegram_bot.field.bot_token.desc: The token you get from @BotFather with /newbot, shaped like 123456:ABC-DEF…. It is kept on this machine only and never uploaded anywhere
plugin.telegram_bot.field.busy_hold.desc: While the character is busy on the agenda or asleep, messages are kept and answered a while later: at most ten minutes when very busy (a quick glance at the phone), once the activity ends when the character cannot reply at all, and after the time below when asleep. The turn that answers tells the character how long ago the message was sent. Commands are unaffected
plugin.telegram_bot.field.confirm_timeou: How long a confirmation request waits for /apply or /deny; a timeout counts as a refusal
plugin.telegram_bot.field.format.desc: markdown: converted to Telegram MarkdownV2, so bold and code blocks render properly, falling back to plain text for that user if parsing fails. Plain text: always converted to readable plain text first
plugin.telegram_bot.field.format.label: Message format
plugin.telegram_bot.field.human_pace.des: Splits a reply into several messages by sentence, sends them with typing pauses in between, and asks the model to talk the way people text (short sentences, spoken register, no formatting). Command receipts, confirmation requests and progress notes still arrive as one message
plugin.telegram_bot.field.merge_window_s: Several messages sent by the same person within this window are merged into one turn before replying, the way a person waits for the other to finish; each new message restarts the clock, and the total wait never exceeds three windows. 0 turns it off and replies to each. Commands are unaffected
plugin.telegram_bot.field.proxy.desc: api.telegram.org is unreachable directly on some networks. http, https and socks5 are supported, shaped like socks5://127.0.0.1:1080 or http://127.0.0.1:7890; leave it empty to connect directly
plugin.telegram_bot.field.proxy.label: Proxy address
plugin.telegram_bot.field.push_notices.d: Also push the notes background work leaves behind (what a memory distillation recorded, for instance). Only shared content is pushed, and pushing writes nothing to the session
Also push each turn's reasoning (it can be long)
plugin.telegram_bot.field.show_tools.des: Also push which tools each turn called (names only, no arguments or results)
plugin.telegram_bot.field.stream_preview: While a reply is still being generated, show what has been written so far in the chat (Telegram's draft preview, replaced by the real message when done). With it on, replies stop feeling like a person typing: nobody lets you watch their words appear one by one
Show replies as they are written
plugin.telegram_bot.field.wake_after_min: With "Reply later when busy" on, messages that arrive while the character is asleep wake them up after this long, or sooner if they would wake up on their own first. 0 means the first message wakes them; a very long value comes close to "reply once awake"
plugin.telegram_bot.field.whitelist.desc: One chat_id per line (in a one-to-one chat this is your numeric user ID). Only listed users get a reply, and an empty list refuses everyone. Send the bot a message and its chat_id appears in the log
plugin.telegram_bot.msg.unsupported: That message type is not supported yet; please send text.
plugin.unspoken.action.clear.desc: Wipe every unspoken thought, including the separate copies each persona keeps. Cannot be undone.
plugin.unspoken.action.clear.label: Clear unspoken thoughts
plugin.unspoken.clear.failed: Failed to clear the unspoken list: %s
plugin.unspoken.desc: Unspoken: what the character has not said out loud — what it really thinks, what it is holding back, what it is waiting for — kept as a bounded list injected each turn that shapes its attitude and subtext without ever being read aloud
plugin.unspoken.field.max_entries.desc: How many things it can hold at once. When full, the oldest is let go automatically and the model is told so in the receipt.
plugin.unspoken.field.max_entries.label: Entry limit
plugin.unspoken.field.max_inject_bytes.d: The list is resent every turn, so it needs a ceiling. Over the limit, only the most recent entries are kept and the rest are noted as a count.
plugin.unspoken.no_state_dir: No writable directory is available, so what you are thinking cannot be saved
plugin.weather.action.no_city: Fill in a city before testing

plugin.weather.action.test.label: Test these cities
plugin.weather.desc: Weather: fetches the real weather for the configured cities on a timer and injects it each turn as part of the character's surroundings
plugin.weather.err.stale_lt_refresh: "Age at which weather stops being injected" (%d minutes) cannot be smaller than "Refresh interval" (%d minutes): a reading would then be stale the moment it arrived, so nothing would ever be injected
plugin.weather.field.persona_location.de: Where the character lives, such as "Hangzhou" or "杭州". The weather on its side becomes part of its surroundings and its state. Leave it empty to inject nothing.
plugin.weather.field.refresh_minutes.des: How often to fetch in the background. Fetching more often does not produce fresher data, only more calls.
plugin.weather.field.same_city.desc: You are both in the same place. With this on, only the city above is queried and "city I am in" below has no effect.
plugin.weather.field.same_city.label: Same city as me
plugin.weather.field.stale_minutes.desc: Stop injecting weather this long after the last successful fetch. When nothing fresh can be had, it is better for the character not to know the weather than to treat a few hours ago as now. Must not be smaller than the refresh interval.
plugin.weather.field.stale_minutes.label: Stop injecting after (minutes)
From this hour on, tomorrow's forecast is in front of the character — during the day people think about today, and only look ahead near bedtime or when planning. Before that hour it glances at tomorrow only when you bring it up. 0 keeps it visible all day.
Hour to start looking at tomorrow
plugin.weather.field.user_location.desc: Where you are when the two of you are apart; the character knows what the weather is like on your side. Only in effect when the setting above is off; leave it empty to inject nothing.
plugin.weather.field.user_location.label: City I am in
plugin.weather.no_state_dir: No writable directory is available, so weather readings cannot be saved
